thesis: The speakers discuss a two-year study analyzing every economic crisis since 1970, defined as periods where high-yield spreads exceeded 650 basis points. They argue that during such crises, the breadth of rational beliefs expands significantly, meaning a wide range of forecasts cannot be rationally disproven, as illustrated by historical quotes from market bottoms.
